# Solo Satoshi Web Flasher

> A free web flasher for verified Bitaxe, BitForge, NerdAxe, and NerdNOS firmware releases, the Bitaxe Turbo Touch display controller, and local ESP32-S3 images.

## Primary page

- [Solo Satoshi Web Flasher](https://flash.solosatoshi.com/): Use Verified releases for approved upstream firmware or Advanced for a local merged ESP32-S3 image.

## Guides

- [Firmware guides](https://flash.solosatoshi.com/guides/): Practical guides for supported AxeOS and Nerd*OS hardware.
- [How to Update Bitaxe and NerdAxe Firmware](https://flash.solosatoshi.com/guides/bitaxe-firmware-update/): USB connection, exact hardware matching, verified releases, settings preservation, recovery, and post-update checks, with real interface screenshots.

## Documentation and policies

- [Privacy Policy](https://flash.solosatoshi.com/privacy.html): Browser permissions, local files, issue reports, hosting providers, storage, and USB data practices.
- [Terms of Service](https://flash.solosatoshi.com/terms.html): User responsibilities, verified and custom firmware limitations, installation risks, warranties, and liability.
- [Licenses and Source](https://flash.solosatoshi.com/licenses.html): Application, firmware, library, font, upstream-project, and GPL source information.
- [Application source](https://flash.solosatoshi.com/source/latest.tar.gz): GPL-3.0-only corresponding source for the deployed browser application.

## Authoritative facts

- Verified releases discovers approved releases from bitaxeorg/ESP-Miner, WantClue/forge-os, shufps/ESP-Miner-NerdQAxePlus, and bitaxeorg/BAP-GT-TOUCH. NerdNOS uses an explicitly pinned official image and matching source commit.
- Supported Bitaxe models include Max, Ultra, UltraHex, Supra, Gamma, Gamma Duo, SupraHex, Gamma Turbo, GammaHex, and Naja Duo. BitForge Nano and NerdNOS are automatically matched. Supported NerdAxe models include NerdAxe, NerdAxe Gamma, NerdEKO, NerdHaxe Gamma, NerdOCTAXE Gamma, NerdOCTAXE+, NerdQAxe+, NerdQAxe++, NerdQX, Q1370, and Q1373.
- The verified installer shows the newest stable release plus up to five previous stable releases only when a release contains a factory image for the selected board. Firmware from before a hardware model's first supported release is not offered for that model.
- An eligible prerelease is offered only when it is newer than the current stable release. Otherwise the prerelease option remains visible but disabled and Latest Releases is selected automatically.
- Release automation checks the approved repository, asset name, file size, and SHA-256 digest published by GitHub. The browser verifies size and SHA-256 before writing, and the ESP flashing library verifies the completed write.
- Turbo Touch is a screen-only target. Its firmware updates the display controller and does not update the Bitaxe GT miner inside the unit.
- Verified ESP releases may preserve the designated NVS settings partition. The option is off by default and is not a backup.
- Advanced requires an approved USB serial connection before accepting a local merged, bootable ESP32-S3 `.bin` for address `0x0`. The browser checks basic image structure and the connected chip type. The image remains local, is never uploaded, is not authenticated or checked for hardware compatibility, and is written without preserving settings.
- After an ESP flash, the interface reports: firmware written and verified, device restarting, serial connection released, and reset sequence finished. This sequence confirms the flash and reset flow, not mining or network operation after boot.
- USB communication and selected custom firmware remain between the browser and the locally selected device. Technical logs are not uploaded.
- Report an issue sends the reply email and description entered by the user. The email is used only to respond about that report and is not added to a marketing list or separate flasher contact database. Security and bot-protection services protect the submission, and an email provider delivers and stores the support email.
- The application requires a current supported desktop Chrome, Edge, or Brave browser. Phones, tablets, Safari, and Firefox are not supported for flashing.
- The application does not require an account or use advertising analytics. Optional cookieless usage and visit analytics are isolated from firmware files, USB data, and support-form text. Saved declines, Do Not Track, and Global Privacy Control disable optional tracking. The regional consent policy keeps tracking off until accepted outside the United States and in unknown regions; US tracking is on by default unless a saved choice or privacy signal prevents it.
- Detailed usage-analytics logs are configured for deletion after 744 days. Aggregated usage reports and visit analytics have no fixed automatic deletion date. Support correspondence is deleted manually as needed, subject to applicable privacy rights and legal obligations.
- The guides are static, readable HTML with native text instructions, matching FAQs, and original screenshot links. Example device versions and readings are identification and interface examples, not universal firmware recommendations or performance targets.
